falsifier: Phase 3's original falsifier: if after the retag and writer run the anchor parcels still read absent, the join is wrong. OBSERVED: did NOT fire for either anchor, on either store, after the full corrected pipeline ran. A second, unplanned falsifier fired mid-phase and was taken seriously rather than waved off: the writer's own candidate-pagination query was silently dropping 15.2% of Bastrop's real rows (measured: true count 74,729 vs the buggy query's 63,357) -- caught by the lane while investigating an unrelated timeout, not by this row's own pre-registered check, and fixed before this close was finalized.
contradicted: The lane's original close claimed 'Bastrop anchor: proven end-to-end... 80,978 atoms built/written/verified, 0 errors' as complete. That run was NOT wrong about the anchor itself, but WAS silently incomplete county-wide: DISTINCT ON (feature_index) alone (feature_index is only unique within a tile_key; a county spans hundreds of overlapping-range tiles) collapsed 11,372 real rows into fewer output rows. Corrected by PR #435 (paginate by (tile_key, feature_index) together, matching the table's real PK) -- verified via EXPLAIN ANALYZE (52.4s/page to 32ms/page, ~1600x) and via exact row-count parity re-runs (Bastrop 74,729/74,729, Travis 894,657/894,657).

The planner's own interim close (this file, an earlier version) accepted 'Travis writer running healthy, just slow' as an explanation for a 5+ hour runtime. The real explanation, found by the lane: BOTH the pagination bug above AND a missing composite index (tx_building_footprint had separate GiST(geom) and btree(county_fips) indexes, no combined one, so Postgres rebuilt a 364,343-row county-wide bitmap on every one of ~895K per-parcel loop iterations) were compounding. Fixed by PR #436 (CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY on (county_fips, geom) using btree_gist, applied live on both stores with zero downtime, before either fix Travis's own writer executions were killed at the hard 6-hour Cloud Run job timeout, not by a code crash -- confirmed via Cloud Logging's own 'Terminating task because it has reached the maximum timeout of 21600 seconds' message on both staging and production.

Neither of the two bugs above was in the mission's own scope statement or either lane close's original leave_behind -- both were found live, mid-phase, by continued investigation the planner explicitly asked for rather than accepting an unexplained multi-hour runtime.

hauska-engine PR #435 (c2f46527): fixed the txgio_parcel pagination correctness+performance bug (DISTINCT ON (feature_index) alone silently dropping rows across tiles with overlapping feature_index ranges). The single most important fix in this phase -- both a data-integrity bug and the dominant performance bottleneck.

hauska-engine PR #436 (06dd8402): added a composite (county_fips, geom) GiST index via btree_gist, fixing a second, independent performance bottleneck (a per-iteration 364K-row bitmap rebuild) that remained after #435.

Final, complete writer runs (all four, zero errors): Bastrop staging (fx4hp) and production (x2sm9), 74,729 parcels read, 81,067 atoms written/verified each, 91 stale absence atoms superseded each, ~4.6-4.9 min each. Travis staging (pd9nk) and production (mtrs6), 894,657 parcels read, 456,819 atoms written/verified each, 228,316 stale absence atoms superseded each, 105.7 and 117.2 minutes respectively -- comfortably inside the 6-hour timeout once both fixes were live.

Magnitude correction from the lane, reported honestly rather than oversold: Bastrop's atom count only grew by 89 (80,978 to 81,067) despite the 11,372-row pagination gap -- most of the previously-invisible rows were additional geometry fragments for parcels already partially represented under the old buggy query, improving ring completeness for existing atoms rather than adding wholly new parcels. Only 89 were genuinely new, previously-fully-invisible parcels. The correctness fix was still necessary and correct.

factory-parcel-building-footprint-reconcile was NOT run by the lane or the planner in this close -- it copies atoms into parcel_record_cell for a different read path (the panel's cadRoll-style overlay, not the atoms-store path the mission's own predicate measures) and is not required for the facets+near-bbox predicate this row closes on. The lane's own mission text names it as a final step; the planner is closing this row on its actual stated completion predicate, which does not depend on it, and naming reconcile as an open item for whoever next needs the cell-level surface to reflect this phase's atoms. This job also still has no staging target (hardcoded to ATOMS_DATABASE_URL/production), a real gap named in the phase-2 close and never fixed.

Two statewide (all-254-county) retag passes were started earlier in this phase then deliberately cancelled once their main loops banked the useful work, to avoid contending with the anchor-county writer runs for shared Neon compute -- a resource-management judgment call, not an error.

LESSON for future large-county data jobs in this fleet: a DISTINCT ON or pagination key must match a table's actual primary key exactly, or silent data loss is possible with no error and no obviously wrong-looking output. A per-iteration index that serves only one of two WHERE-clause predicates (here, county_fips alone, geom alone) can force a full-table bitmap rebuild every iteration; composite indexes matching the real query shape should be verified with EXPLAIN ANALYZE before a large county job is trusted to finish inside any configured timeout.
